deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes on 'topologie modérée' (tame topology), probably carried out for compact subsets of cubes I^n with a tame class of functions (semialgebraic, semi-analytic or similar). This page seems to check a stability axiom: tame spaces should be closed under attaching or contracting along closed subspaces.

Setup: X ⊂ Y closed (both tame, embedded in cubes) and p: X → Z a tame map. The aim is to embed the pushout Y ⊔_X Z in a cube, i.e. to find a commutative square X→Y, Z→I^n with Z→I^n an embedding and conditions a) b) c).

Step a). Choose an embedding f=(f_1,…,f_p): Z → I^p. Extend each f_α∘p from X to a function g_α: Y → I (a Tietze-type extension in the tame class), so that f_α∘p = g_α∘i. 'Ok pour a)': the square commutes.

Step b). Choose g_{p+1},…,g_{p+q}: Y → I that vanish on X and have common zero set exactly X: ⋂_β g_{p+β}^{-1}(0) = X. On Z put f_{p+β}=0, i.e. σ = 0: Z → I^q. Then f_{p+β}∘p = 0 = g_{p+β}∘i. Read 'card.' as 'cart.': the square X→Y over e→I^q is cartesian, meaning X is the fibre over 0. 'Ok pour b)'.

Key condition. He writes Y ×_{I^q} Y = Δ_Y ∪ (X×X). This says the map Y → I^q is injective off X and collapses X to a point, i.e. Y/X embeds in I^q. This is exactly what the previous page arranges. There, from φ (vanishing exactly on X) and an embedding ψ: Y→I^m, he forms the coordinates (φ_i, φ_iψ_j) using the 'blow-down' (x,y) ↦ (x,xy), which is injective for x≠0 and crushes {x=0}.

Final assembly. Set S = I^{p+q} and S' = I^q, with Y→S, Z→S, and the projection S→S'. From Y ×_{S'} Y = Δ_Y ∪ X×X one deduces Y ×_S Y = Δ_Y ∪ (X ×_Z X), because on X the S-coordinates are f∘p and f is injective. So the image of Y in S is the pushout Y ⊔_X Z, with Z ⊂ S embedded. The quotient topology is correct by compactness.

In modern terms: existence of tame (definable) quotients / adjunction spaces Y ∪_X Z for closed X, via explicit embeddings into cubes.
errors: On this page Y ×_{I^q} Y = Δ_Y ∪ (X×X) does not follow merely from g_{p+β} having common zero set X; that only gives the fibre over 0. Injectivity off X needs the extra coordinates g_{p+β}·ψ_j from the previous page (the (x,y)↦(x,xy) trick), which enlarges q. Presumably intended, but not written here.

Step a) silently uses a Tietze extension theorem within the tame class, and the homeomorphism onto the image uses compactness (closed subsets of cubes) or properness. Both are true in the semialgebraic/o-minimal setting but unproved here.
'∨' is used for union of subsets (Δ_Y ∪ X×X).

ideas.what: Embedding the contraction Y/X (X closed) into a cube via coordinates (φ, φ·ψ), where φ has zero set X and ψ is an embedding
ideas.modern_name: Definable/semialgebraic quotient by a closed subset (cone/blow-down trick)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Robson, 'Embedding semi-algebraic spaces' (Math. Z. 1983); Brumfiel 1987; van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal structures (1998), ch. 10
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5, lists stability of tame spaces under such quotients/gluings as a desideratum; the explicit construction is not given there as far as I know

ideas.what: Embedding the pushout Y ⊔_X Z by combining an extension of f∘p with the collapsing map, checked via fibre products Y×_S Y = Δ ∪ X×_Z X
ideas.modern_name: Existence of definable adjunction spaces (gluing along proper definable maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Robson 1983; Delfs–Knebusch (locally semialgebraic spaces, 1985); van den Dries 1998

ideas.what: Characterising injectivity modulo an equivalence relation by the fibre product Y×_S Y equalling Δ ∪ (X×_Z X)
ideas.modern_name: Effective equivalence relation / kernel pair computation
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 / FGA style descent of equivalence relations (general method)

missed.claim: By 1974 Grothendieck had an explicit, essentially complete construction showing that a compact tame subset of a cube, with a closed subset X attached to Z via p: X→Z, has its adjunction space again embeddable in a cube. This anticipates Robson (1983) and van den Dries's treatment of definable quotients.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it shows the stability axiom stated in the Esquisse (1984) had been checked by hand a decade earlier, with essentially the same argument later used in semialgebraic/o-minimal geometry. Mathematically it is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is correct and anticipates published work on semialgebraic/definable quotients (Robson 1983, van den Dries 1998) by about a decade. The result itself is now standard and the argument is elementary, so it is mainly of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'card.' should likely be read 'cart.' (cartesian square: X is the fibre of Y→I^q over 0).
'f_1 - f_n : Z → I' introduces the embedding coordinates; later indices run to p (f_1…f_p, then f_{p+1}…f_{p+q}).
In 'f_α ∘ p = g_α ∘ i / 1≤α≤p   Y → I', the 'Y → I' indicates g_α: Y → I.
'hen[?]' after '= X' is illegible; possibly 'bien' or 'déf.'.
